newsitem.title: UK: Major calls sleaze allegations "total junk".
newsitem.headline: Major calls sleaze allegations "total junk".

text.p: LONDON, March 21 - Prime Minister John Major said on Friday the latest sleaze allegations printed in the Guardian newspaper were "total and complete junk".
Major, speaking to reporters ahead of a May 1 election, angrily denounced the latest sleaze charges to hit his government as "nonsense" and said there was nothing new in the allegations.
"It's total and complete junk. And what is more the Guardian should have known it," he said.
"It's not a fresh matter," he said.

Earlier Major's Downing Street office denied the Guardian newspaper charges that the prime minister allowed ruling party MP Tim Smith to continue as a junior minister in 1994 after he was told of allegations that Smith took cash to ask questions in parliament.
